text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert auto-fired: PD# PD-11723 — HTTP 5xx rate > threshold in inference-gateway (eu-west1). Trigger: error_rate > 5% for 2m. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-11723

pagerduty: Paging: emily (oncall) — escalation policy: inference-prod. Please acknowledge.

emily (oncall): acked. Looking now. Which customers impacted?

raj: quick signal check — we're seeing a ~12% 5xx rate in eu-west1 for /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Spike started ~08:12 UTC. Baseline is ~0.3%.

jordan: logs look like backend 502/503 from inference-gateway -> runtime pool. Example tail from gateway logs:

```
2026-03-14T08:13:04Z gateway[eu-west1] ERROR request_id=abc123 upstream_status=502 upstream_host=10.2.5.17 msg="upstream returned 502"
2026-03-14T08:13:05Z gateway[eu-west1] ERROR request_id=abc124 upstream_status=502 kv_cache_miss=true
```

maria: customer-impact quick check: Support tickets coming from two midsize customers in EU; both report intermittent "502" responses in prod. No high-revenue customers flagged yet.

emily (oncall): thanks. Can we fail open to a cheaper model in other regions and reduce batching to cut per-request memory pressure? Also enable rate-limiter backpressure so retries don't amplify.

raj: trying routing fallback to model-compat small variant (cpu/qat) and divert 30% of EU traffic to us-east1 for now. Running router change: 

```
# redirect 30% eu-west1 -> us-east1 for model=redwood-compat-small
redwoodctl routes apply --from-region eu-west1 --to-region us-east1 --model redwood-compat-small --percent 30 --reason "auto-pager mitigation"
```

jordan: also toggled dynamic-batch max_tokens from 2048 to 512 for eu runtime pools to reduce mem spikes. Command: 

```
redwoodctl runtime update --pool eu-runtime-1 --dynamic-batch-max 512
```

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook: Inference 5xx spike — steps executed: acknowledged -> apply fallback model -> reduce batch size -> warm KV-cache (if applicable) -> monitor 10m. Docs: https://runbooks.internal/inference-5xx

emily (oncall): issuing temporary customer notice via status page? We should preempt tickets.

maria: I'll draft a short status with "partial degradation in EU — intermittent 502s — mitigation in progress; no data loss" and post to status.redwood.ai.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback executed for last autoscaled runtime snapshot: rollback id=rel-2026-03-14-2026c -> rolled back 3 instances in eu-west1.

raj: after routing + batch changes + rollback, error rate dropped from 12% -> 2.1% in 4m. Still above baseline but trending down.

emily (oncall): great. Keep routing fallback in place for 20m then re-evaluate. Also open an incident ticket for postmortem and assign action items.

jordan: capturing a few suspicious traces — increased latency + OOM logs on a subset of runtime VMs right before the 502 burst. Likely memory pressure from a recent model change in the pool.

maria: status page posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/PD-11723 — added note to contact support if experiencing continued errors.

emily (oncall): escalation: if rate > 5% again in next 15m, escalate to senior oncall (raj-sr). For now, moving to watch. Anyone else doing customer callbacks?

maria: support will prioritize the two affected accounts; assigning urgent follow-up.

raj: monitoring graphs: 5xx rate EU: https://grafana.redwood/graph?panel=503_eu — KV-cache hitrate stable after fallback. Will keep an eye on memory metrics: VM mem% and oom_kill_count.

sre-runbook-bot: Note: remind to collect heap profiles from runtime if OOM suspected: run: 
```
redwoodctl debug heapdump --pool eu-runtime-1 --since 08:00Z --out /tmp/heap-eu-08-14.tar.gz
```

deploy-bot: New deploy prevented (safety gate) while incident active: locks applied to eu-runtime-1.

emily (oncall): we're trending to normal. Last check: error rate 0.9% in eu and routed traffic still at 30% to us-east1. Can we start draining us-east1 fallback after 25m?

raj: agree. Scheduling rollback of fallback at 08:40 UTC if metrics stable <1%.

jordan: filed an internal bug: probable memory leak with large request sequences; ticket INF-5621 created and assigned to eng-runtime.

emily (oncall): closing pager on PD once elevated watch period is over. I'll create the incident doc with timeline and mitigation steps. Follow-ups: (1) root cause triage with runtime team, (2) add pre-emptive health-checks for batch OOMs, (3) improve runbook automated fallback percentages.

maria: support callbacks queued and customers notified. Will add case refs in incident doc.

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert resolved: PD-11723 — status: acknowledged -> resolved by emily (oncall). Duration: 28m.

emily (oncall): incident resolved. Will post a short summary in #postmortems and link to the incident doc. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
